title: Rabbit
intro: Rabbit begins by celebrating inactivity, then exposes the effort underneath avoiding people. A bed is reliable, while social warmth can be unreturned and confident manners can conceal bad intentions. The speaker's retreat therefore protects both comfort and dignity. But the ending reverses his opening wish to be left alone: he demands truth from others under threat. The song traces how disappointment can turn a desire for less contact into a desire to control the contact that remains, without making that demand a solution to mistrust.
reading: Voluntary idleness gives way to defensive withdrawal, then coercive demands that cannot guarantee sincerity.

revisions.35-n4: Doing nothing initially feels good. The clipped list then introduces exhaustion, bad mood and a demand not to be looked at. The later explanation of humiliating social effort changes how we hear the opening: drifting is a pleasure, but also relief from encounters that cost more than they return. Neither pure laziness nor pure suffering captures the movement between those states.
revisions.editorial-35-bed-escort: The bed helps him into sleep reliably and on time. The personification supplies a small model of dependable care before the verse describes people whose words cannot be trusted. An object does not make him audition for its warmth or repay a social debt. That contrast explains the attraction of staying in more precisely than a generic dislike of going outside.
revisions.35-n1: The warm face pressed against a cold backside makes unanswered friendliness bodily humiliating. He also says they barely know each other, so the issue is not necessarily a lost intimate bond. It is the expectation that he should perform eagerness without reciprocal welcome. Refusing that performance protects dignity, even as the later generalisation that everyone conceals something hardens a particular frustration into suspicion of the whole scene.
revisions.editorial-35-honest-words: The demand for words from the heart ends in a threat to hit whoever withholds them. That cannot secure the sincerity it wants: frightened people have a new reason to say what will satisfy the threatening person. The contradiction is a destination of the song, not a loose end the annotation should repair. The speaker who wanted freedom from social demands has begun issuing a particularly forceful one himself.
